chapters.reason: The paper proposes Bit Diffusion, which maps discrete data to continuous embeddings (analog bits) and uses a continuous diffusion model with Gaussian noise to denoise them, fitting the description of embedding-based diffusion models.

While the core method is embedding-based, the paper discusses generating discrete data (like images and captions) which relates to the domain of masked diffusion models, but the approach is not based on token masking.

The paper compares its diffusion approach to autoregressive models in terms of performance, but it does not integrate AR and diffusion paradigms; it is a pure diffusion method, making this a distant match.
